Under the joint law of a uniform message among M ≥ 1, its encoded word, and the channel output, these variables form a Markov chain in that order.
For M ≥ 1 and a uniform message, the message, received word and decoded estimate form a Markov chain in that order.
For M ≥ 1 and a uniform message J, decoding the received word Y can only reduce its mutual information with J, so I(J;decoder(Y)) ≤ I(J;Y).
For a finite-alphabet block code and M ≥ 1, the mutual information between the uniform message J and output Y is at most the mutual information between the encoded input X and Y.

Let W have finite alphabets, a nonempty input alphabet and capacity C in nats per use. For any blocklength n ≥ 0 and any code with M ≥ 1 equiprobable messages, the average error e satisfies (1 − e) ln M ≤ nC + ln 2.
For positive n and M ≥ 1, a code of rate r and average error e on a finite channel of capacity C satisfies (1 − e)r ≤ C + (ln 2)/n.
If n > 0, M ≥ 1 and the code rate is at least R > 0, its average error on a finite channel of capacity C is at least 1 − C/R − (ln 2)/(nR).
